blocks.en: 📖 Deacon Family Ministry Plan — Unit 7: Discipleship and Evangelism within Assigned Families
blocks.es_reference: 📖 Plan de Ministerio Familiar del Diácono — Unidad 7: Discipulado y Evangelismo dentro de las Familias Asignadas

blocks.en: Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Profesor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: "Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit." — Matthew 28:19 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: «Por tanto, id, y enseñad a todas las naciones, bautizándolos en el nombre del Padre, y del Hijo, y del Espíritu Santo.» — Mateo 28:19 (RVG)

blocks.en: In Unit 6 we saw the ongoing care of the deacon — his ministry of visitation and prayer. But that care is never an end in itself. The deacon is not merely a friendly visitor or a kindly social worker; he is a servant of Christ, and his deepest aim for every family in his care is a spiritual one. He longs to see the believers among them grow into strong, mature disciples, and the lost among them come to faith in Christ. Woven through all his visiting and praying, then, are two great spiritual purposes: discipleship and evangelism.
blocks.es_reference: En la Unidad 6 vimos el cuidado continuo del diácono — su ministerio de visitación y oración. Pero ese cuidado nunca es un fin en sí mismo. El diácono no es meramente un visitante amistoso ni un bondadoso trabajador social; es un siervo de Cristo, y su propósito más profundo para cada familia a su cuidado es espiritual. Anhela ver a los creyentes entre ellas crecer hasta ser discípulos fuertes y maduros, y a los perdidos entre ellas venir a la fe en Cristo. Entretejidos, pues, en todo su visitar y orar, hay dos grandes propósitos espirituales: el discipulado y el evangelismo.

blocks.en: Subject: the deacon's ministry of discipleship and evangelism within his assigned families.
blocks.es_reference: Tema: el ministerio del diácono de discipulado y evangelismo dentro de sus familias asignadas.

blocks.en: Proposition: Beyond meeting his families' needs, the deacon labors to make disciples of them — disciples marked by commitment, confession, and a willingness to bear the cost — and to win the lost among them to Christ.
blocks.es_reference: Proposición: Más allá de suplir las necesidades de sus familias, el diácono se esfuerza por hacer discípulos de ellas — discípulos marcados por el compromiso, la confesión, y una disposición a llevar el costo — y por ganar para Cristo a los perdidos entre ellas.

blocks.en: We will consider the three marks of the disciple the deacon seeks to build, and then the evangelistic burden he carries for the lost.
blocks.es_reference: Consideraremos las tres marcas del discípulo que el diácono procura edificar, y luego la carga evangelística que lleva por los perdidos.

blocks.en: I. The Disciple's Mark
blocks.es_reference: I. La Marca del Discípulo

blocks.en: The word “disciple” appears over and over in the New Testament. It means a learner — one who follows the teaching and lifestyle of another. The disciple is not only a pupil; he is an imitator of his teacher. And a true disciple bears his Master's mark.
blocks.es_reference: La palabra «discípulo» aparece una y otra vez en el Nuevo Testamento. Significa un aprendiz — uno que sigue la enseñanza y el estilo de vida de otro. El discípulo no es solo un alumno; es un imitador de su maestro. Y un verdadero discípulo lleva la marca de su Señor.

blocks.en: Illustration. I have at home an old family branding iron, stamped with our name. Years ago my father used it to brand his cattle, and everyone knew the cattle belonged to him because of the mark they bore. In the same way, the disciple of Christ carries the Lord's markings upon him. People can tell whose he is.
blocks.es_reference: Ilustración. Tengo en casa un viejo hierro de marcar de la familia, estampado con nuestro apellido. Hace años mi padre lo usaba para marcar su ganado, y todos sabían que el ganado era suyo por la marca que llevaba. De la misma manera, el discípulo de Cristo lleva las marcas del Señor sobre sí. La gente puede ver de quién es.

blocks.en: The deacon's spiritual aim for his families is exactly this: that every soul among them should bear the unmistakable mark of belonging to Christ. He cares for their bodies and their burdens, but most of all he longs to see them branded as the Lord's own — true disciples. From the words of Christ in Matthew 10 we may draw three marks of such a disciple, and the deacon labors to see all three formed in the families he serves.
blocks.es_reference: El propósito espiritual del diácono para sus familias es exactamente este: que cada alma entre ellas lleve la marca inconfundible de pertenecer a Cristo. Cuida de sus cuerpos y de sus cargas, pero sobre todo anhela verlas marcadas como propiedad del Señor — verdaderos discípulos. De las palabras de Cristo en Mateo 10 podemos sacar tres marcas de tal discípulo, y el diácono se esfuerza por ver las tres formadas en las familias que sirve.

blocks.en: II. The First Mark: Commitment
blocks.es_reference: II. La Primera Marca: el Compromiso

blocks.en: The first mark is commitment. Jesus said we are to love the Lord our God with all our heart, with all our soul, and with all our mind. To declare our love for God is a fine thing, but it means nothing if there is no commitment behind it. The great danger is a religion that is wide but shallow. There is often much interest in God — people who will debate about God, study about God, and seek help from God — while the depth of real commitment remains pathetically thin, like a river a mile wide and an inch deep. The deacon's task is to help lead his families out of shallow interest and into genuine, committed discipleship.
blocks.es_reference: La primera marca es el compromiso. Jesús dijo que hemos de amar al Señor nuestro Dios con todo nuestro corazón, con toda nuestra alma, y con toda nuestra mente. Declarar nuestro amor por Dios es algo bueno, pero no significa nada si no hay compromiso detrás de ello. El gran peligro es una religión ancha pero superficial. A menudo hay mucho interés en Dios — personas que debatirán acerca de Dios, estudiarán acerca de Dios, y buscarán ayuda de Dios — mientras la profundidad del compromiso real permanece lastimosamente delgada, como un río de una milla de ancho y una pulgada de profundidad. La tarea del diácono es ayudar a guiar a sus familias fuera del interés superficial y hacia un discipulado genuino y comprometido.

blocks.en: A committed Christian is an active Christian, one who serves joyfully — not out of duty, not out of guilt, but out of love.
blocks.es_reference: Un cristiano comprometido es un cristiano activo, uno que sirve con gozo — no por deber, no por culpa, sino por amor.

blocks.en: Illustration. In the stagecoach days, a man bought a third-class ticket and congratulated himself on the money he had saved, for all the seats were the same. Then they came to a steep hill. The driver stopped the horses and shouted, “First-class passengers, keep your seats; second-class, get out and walk; third-class, get out and push.” What the church needs is more third-class passengers who will get out and push — not first-class who are content to sit and look on, nor second-class who walk away when the real work begins. The deacon quietly encourages his families to be the kind who push.
blocks.es_reference: Ilustración. En los días de las diligencias, un hombre compró un boleto de tercera clase y se felicitó por el dinero que había ahorrado, pues todos los asientos eran iguales. Entonces llegaron a una cuesta empinada. El conductor detuvo los caballos y gritó: «Pasajeros de primera clase, quédense sentados; los de segunda, bajen y caminen; los de tercera, bajen y empujen.» Lo que la iglesia necesita son más pasajeros de tercera clase que bajen y empujen — no los de primera que se contentan con sentarse y mirar, ni los de segunda que se alejan cuando comienza la obra de veras. El diácono anima calladamente a sus familias a ser de los que empujan.

blocks.en: Such commitment shows itself also in enthusiasm and loyalty — a holy expectancy that looks for great things from God, and a faithfulness to the gathered church. To say one need not gather with the church to be a Christian is rather like saying one need not be faithful to keep a marriage. The deacon models this committed, active, loyal discipleship, and gently calls his families up into it.
blocks.es_reference: Tal compromiso se muestra también en el entusiasmo y la lealtad — una santa expectativa que espera grandes cosas de Dios, y una fidelidad a la iglesia reunida. Decir que uno no necesita reunirse con la iglesia para ser cristiano es algo así como decir que uno no necesita ser fiel para mantener un matrimonio. El diácono modela este discipulado comprometido, activo y leal, y suavemente llama a sus familias a alcanzarlo.

blocks.en: And he calls them up into it chiefly by example. A deacon who is himself only a Sunday Christian will never lift his families higher than he has climbed; but one whose own commitment is plain — in service, in faithfulness, in joy — raises the whole standard simply by living it before them. We reproduce what we are far more than what we say.
blocks.es_reference: Y los llama a alcanzarlo principalmente por el ejemplo. Un diácono que él mismo es solo un cristiano de domingo nunca levantará a sus familias más alto de lo que él ha subido; pero aquel cuyo propio compromiso es evidente — en el servicio, en la fidelidad, en el gozo — eleva toda la norma sencillamente viviéndola delante de ellas. Reproducimos lo que somos mucho más que lo que decimos.

blocks.en: III. The Second Mark: Confession
blocks.es_reference: III. La Segunda Marca: la Confesión

blocks.en: The second mark is confession — the open owning of Christ before others. The Lord Himself made this a dividing line.
blocks.es_reference: La segunda marca es la confesión — el reconocimiento abierto de Cristo delante de otros. El Señor mismo hizo de esto una línea divisoria.

blocks.en: Therefore whoever confesses Me before men, him I will also confess before My Father who is in heaven. But whoever denies Me before men, him I will also deny before My Father who is in heaven. (Matthew 10:32–33, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: Cualquiera, pues, que me confesare delante de los hombres, le confesaré yo también delante de mi Padre que está en los cielos. Y cualquiera que me negare delante de los hombres, le negaré yo también delante de mi Padre que está en los cielos. (Mateo 10:32–33, RVG)

blocks.en: There has always been a pressure to blend in with the crowd and avoid trouble. A well-known man, asked whether he was a Christian, once answered, “Yes, but not offensively so” — meaning that he never let his Christianity interfere with the friends he kept or the pleasures he loved. The true disciple, by contrast, owns Christ openly and without apology. This confession is made in two ways. It is made by the life, for it is impossible to divorce a witness from a lifestyle; in everything he does a believer is either drawing people toward Jesus or driving them away. Why should Christ make a difference in others' lives when He makes no visible difference in our own? And it is made by the lips, for we must not be too timid or ashamed to tell others plainly of the Lord. The deacon helps his families become bold and consistent confessors, whose lives and words alike point to Christ.
blocks.es_reference: Siempre ha habido una presión para mezclarse con la multitud y evitar problemas. Un hombre muy conocido, al preguntársele si era cristiano, respondió una vez: «Sí, pero no de manera ofensiva» — queriendo decir que nunca permitía que su cristianismo interfiriera con los amigos que tenía ni con los placeres que amaba. El verdadero discípulo, por el contrario, reconoce a Cristo abiertamente y sin disculpas. Esta confesión se hace de dos maneras. Se hace con la vida, porque es imposible divorciar el testimonio del estilo de vida; en todo lo que hace, un creyente está atrayendo a las personas hacia Jesús o alejándolas. ¿Por qué habría Cristo de hacer una diferencia en la vida de otros cuando no hace ninguna diferencia visible en la nuestra? Y se hace con los labios, porque no debemos ser demasiado tímidos ni avergonzados para hablar a otros claramente del Señor. El diácono ayuda a sus familias a ser confesores audaces y consecuentes, cuyas vidas y palabras por igual señalan a Cristo.

blocks.en: IV. The Third Mark: Cost
blocks.es_reference: IV. La Tercera Marca: el Costo

blocks.en: The third mark is a willingness to bear the cost, for following Jesus has never been without cost. The world that hated the Master hates His disciples too; Peter reminds us that Christ suffered for us, “leaving us an example, that you should follow His steps” (1 Peter 2:21). That cost may fall in several places. It may touch our families, for Christ warned that He came not to bring peace but a sword, even setting a man at odds with his own household (Matthew 10:34–36); many a new believer has met the hardest opposition at home. It may touch our worldly interests, for if we love anything more than the Lord, He may ask us to lay it down — as He once asked Isaac of Abraham, and all his riches of the rich young ruler. And it may touch even life itself, for Christ said that whoever does not take up his cross and follow Him is not worthy of Him, and that whoever loses his life for His sake will find it (Matthew 10:38–39).
blocks.es_reference: La tercera marca es una disposición a llevar el costo, porque seguir a Jesús nunca ha sido sin costo. El mundo que odió al Maestro odia también a sus discípulos; Pedro nos recuerda que Cristo padeció por nosotros, «dejándonos ejemplo, para que sigáis sus pisadas» (1 Pedro 2:21). Ese costo puede caer en varios lugares. Puede tocar a nuestras familias, porque Cristo advirtió que no vino a traer paz sino espada, poniendo aun a un hombre en contra de su propia casa (Mateo 10:34–36); muchos creyentes nuevos han hallado la oposición más dura en su propio hogar. Puede tocar nuestros intereses mundanos, porque si amamos algo más que al Señor, Él puede pedirnos que lo dejemos — como una vez le pidió a Abraham a Isaac, y al joven rico todas sus riquezas. Y puede tocar aun la vida misma, porque Cristo dijo que el que no toma su cruz y le sigue no es digno de Él, y que el que pierde su vida por causa de Él la hallará (Mateo 10:38–39).

blocks.en: Illustration. When the ship Empress of Ireland went down with many Salvation Army officers aboard, the survivors told how those officers, finding there were not enough life belts for all, took off their own and strapped them onto others — even onto strong men — saying, “I can die better than you can.” Of the bodies later recovered, not one wore a life belt. That is a disciple who has counted the cost.
blocks.es_reference: Ilustración. Cuando el barco Empress of Ireland se hundió con muchos oficiales del Ejército de Salvación a bordo, los sobrevivientes contaron cómo aquellos oficiales, al hallar que no había suficientes salvavidas para todos, se quitaron los suyos y los amarraron a otros — aun a hombres fuertes — diciendo: «Yo puedo morir mejor que tú.» De los cuerpos recuperados después, ni uno llevaba salvavidas. Ese es un discípulo que ha contado el costo.

blocks.en: The deacon prepares and strengthens his families to count this cost honestly, so that they will follow Christ even when it is hard and even when it is costly. A disciple who has counted the cost beforehand will not fall away when the trouble comes.
blocks.es_reference: El diácono prepara y fortalece a sus familias para contar este costo honestamente, de modo que sigan a Cristo aun cuando sea difícil y aun cuando sea costoso. Un discípulo que ha contado el costo de antemano no caerá cuando venga la dificultad.

blocks.en: This is why honest teaching about the cost is itself an act of love. A deacon who promises his families an easy, comfortable Christianity sets them up to stumble at the first hardship; but one who tells them the truth — that the path is glorious but not always easy — gives them roots that will hold. He does not frighten them away from Christ; he prepares them to follow Him all the way home.
blocks.es_reference: Por esto la enseñanza honesta acerca del costo es en sí misma un acto de amor. Un diácono que promete a sus familias un cristianismo fácil y cómodo las prepara para tropezar a la primera dificultad; pero el que les dice la verdad — que el camino es glorioso pero no siempre fácil — les da raíces que sostendrán. No las asusta alejándolas de Cristo; las prepara para seguirle todo el camino a casa.

blocks.en: V. Seeking the Lost: The Deacon as Soul-Winner
blocks.es_reference: V. Buscando a los Perdidos: el Diácono como Ganador de Almas

blocks.en: The deacon labors to build disciples — committed, confessing, and ready to bear the cost. But his spiritual work has a second great aim: he also seeks the lost among his families, that they too may come to Christ. We must never assume that everyone already knows the Lord; most do not. And the deacon shares his Master's own heart:
blocks.es_reference: El diácono se esfuerza por edificar discípulos — comprometidos, confesantes, y listos para llevar el costo. Pero su obra espiritual tiene un segundo gran objetivo: también busca a los perdidos entre sus familias, para que ellos también vengan a Cristo. Nunca debemos suponer que todos ya conocen al Señor; la mayoría no. Y el diácono comparte el corazón mismo de su Maestro:

blocks.en: For the Son of Man has come to seek and to save that which was lost. (Luke 19:10, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: Porque el Hijo del Hombre vino a buscar y a salvar lo que se había perdido. (Lucas 19:10, RVG)

blocks.en: The deacon is uniquely placed to reach the lost, because most people come to Christ not through a stranger but through a friend. Of the many people healed by Jesus in the Gospels, the great majority were brought to Him by others; only a handful found their way to Him alone. So it is still: people are most often brought to Jesus by those who already know and love them. The deacon, who knows his families and has earned their trust, is exactly such a friend — and, being a layman, he often has an access that no preacher enjoys.
blocks.es_reference: El diácono está en una posición única para alcanzar a los perdidos, porque la mayoría de las personas vienen a Cristo no por medio de un extraño sino por medio de un amigo. De las muchas personas sanadas por Jesús en los Evangelios, la gran mayoría fueron traídas a Él por otros; solo unos pocos hallaron el camino a Él por sí solos. Así sigue siendo: las personas son traídas a Jesús, las más de las veces, por los que ya las conocen y las aman. El diácono, que conoce a sus familias y se ha ganado su confianza, es precisamente tal amigo — y, siendo un laico, a menudo tiene un acceso del que ningún predicador goza.

blocks.en: Illustration. A plumber in Texas carried a New Testament alongside his tools and became known as the “witnessing plumber.” A minister said of him, “That witnessing plumber has won hundreds to Christ since he became a Christian. Many will listen to a workingman who will not listen to a preacher.” The deacon is just such a workingman among workingmen; his families, and their relatives and neighbors, will often hear the gospel from him as they would from no one else.
blocks.es_reference: Ilustración. Un plomero en Texas llevaba un Nuevo Testamento junto a sus herramientas y llegó a ser conocido como el «plomero que testificaba.» Un ministro dijo de él: «Ese plomero que testifica ha ganado a cientos para Cristo desde que se hizo cristiano. Muchos escucharán a un obrero que no escucharían a un predicador.» El diácono es justamente tal obrero entre obreros; sus familias, y sus parientes y vecinos, a menudo oirán el evangelio de él como no lo oirían de ningún otro.

blocks.en: So the deacon watches for open doors, builds the relationship, and speaks of Christ — personally, lovingly, and plainly. He prays for the lost by name. He remembers that his families' unsaved loved ones will one day face eternity, and that Jesus is not merely an answer but the only answer. And, like Andrew who first brought his brother Simon to Jesus (John 1:41–42), he brings them to the Savior, for how shall they believe in Him of whom they have not heard (Romans 10:14)? This is evangelism within the Plan — not a cold program of strangers, but the natural overflow of a deacon who loves the souls in his care too much to let them perish.
blocks.es_reference: Así que el diácono vela por las puertas abiertas, edifica la relación, y habla de Cristo — personal, amorosa y claramente. Ora por los perdidos por nombre. Recuerda que los seres queridos no salvos de sus familias un día enfrentarán la eternidad, y que Jesús no es meramente una respuesta sino la única respuesta. Y, como Andrés que primero trajo a su hermano Simón a Jesús (Juan 1:41–42), los trae al Salvador, porque ¿cómo creerán en Aquel de quien no han oído (Romanos 10:14)? Esto es evangelismo dentro del Plan — no un programa frío de extraños, sino el desborde natural de un diácono que ama demasiado las almas a su cuidado como para dejarlas perecer.

blocks.en: Such evangelism is usually patient work. The deacon may sow for years before he reaps, praying and loving and waiting while the seed takes root in a hard heart. He need not be pushy, but neither may he be silent; he simply keeps the door open, keeps the relationship warm, and keeps speaking of Christ as the Spirit gives opportunity. In the end it is God who saves; but He is pleased to use a faithful friend to bring the lost within reach of His grace.
blocks.es_reference: Tal evangelismo es por lo general una obra paciente. El diácono puede sembrar por años antes de segar, orando y amando y esperando mientras la semilla echa raíces en un corazón duro. No necesita ser insistente, pero tampoco puede callar; sencillamente mantiene la puerta abierta, mantiene cálida la relación, y sigue hablando de Cristo conforme el Espíritu da la oportunidad. Al final es Dios quien salva; pero le place usar a un amigo fiel para traer a los perdidos al alcance de su gracia.

blocks.en: Conclusion
blocks.es_reference: Conclusión

blocks.en: The deacon's care reaches all the way to the soul. He visits and he prays, as Unit 6 showed; but he also disciples and evangelizes, longing to see every person in his families bear the Lord's mark — the saved growing into committed, confessing, cross-bearing disciples, and the lost brought home to Christ. This is the highest reach of the whole Plan. A deacon might meet every physical need a family has and still have failed them, if he never cared for their souls; but the deacon who makes disciples and wins the lost is doing the very work of Christ, who came to seek and to save.
blocks.es_reference: El cuidado del diácono llega hasta el alma misma. Visita y ora, como mostró la Unidad 6; pero también discipula y evangeliza, anhelando ver a cada persona en sus familias llevar la marca del Señor — los salvos creciendo hasta ser discípulos comprometidos, confesantes y portadores de la cruz, y los perdidos traídos a casa a Cristo. Este es el alcance más alto de todo el Plan. Un diácono podría suplir cada necesidad física que una familia tenga y aun así haberle fallado, si nunca cuidó de sus almas; pero el diácono que hace discípulos y gana a los perdidos está haciendo la obra misma de Cristo, que vino a buscar y a salvar.

blocks.en: “Go therefore and make disciples,” the Lord commanded. The faithful deacon obeys that great commission not among far-off nations, but among the handful of families entrusted to his care. With this, the heart of his spiritual work is set. Yet those same families will also pass through deep waters — sickness, tragedy, and hard secrets — and how the deacon ministers in crisis, guards what is told him in confidence, and knows when to call for help is the subject we take up in Unit 8.
blocks.es_reference: «Por tanto, id, y enseñad a todas las naciones» (es decir, haced discípulos), mandó el Señor. El diácono fiel obedece esa gran comisión no entre naciones lejanas, sino entre el puñado de familias confiadas a su cuidado. Con esto, el corazón de su obra espiritual queda establecido. Sin embargo, esas mismas familias también pasarán por aguas profundas — enfermedad, tragedia, y secretos difíciles — y cómo el diácono ministra en la crisis, guarda lo que se le dice en confianza, y sabe cuándo pedir ayuda es el tema que tomamos en la Unidad 8.

fill.prompt: In the New Testament the word "disciple" means ____: one who follows the teaching and lifestyle of another.
Just as the branded cattle showed whose they were, a true disciple bears his Master's ____.
The first mark of the disciple is ____, the solid backing that must stand behind our declared love for God, or that love means nothing.
The great danger is a religion that is wide but ____, like a river a mile wide and an inch deep.
The church needs more third-class passengers who will get out and ____.
The second mark of the disciple is ____, the open owning of Christ before others.
The third mark of the disciple is a willingness to bear the ____, for following Jesus has never been without it.
"For the Son of Man has come to seek and to ____ that which was lost" (Luke 19:10).
Of the witnessing plumber it was said, "Many will listen to a workingman who will not listen to a ____."
Like ____, who first brought his brother Simon to Jesus (John 1:41–42), the deacon brings the lost to the Savior.

sa.prompt: What are the deacon's two great spiritual aims for his families?
sa.model: The deacon's two great spiritual aims for his families are discipleship and evangelism. He is not merely a friendly visitor or a social worker but a servant of Christ, so his deepest concern for every family is spiritual. By discipleship he labors to see the believers among them grow into strong, mature disciples, marked by commitment, confession, and a willingness to bear the cost. By evangelism he seeks the lost among them, that they too may come to faith in Christ. Both purposes are woven through all his ordinary visiting and praying.

sa.prompt: What is a disciple, and what does the branding iron teach about him?
sa.model: A disciple is a learner, one who follows the teaching and lifestyle of another; he is not only a pupil but an imitator of his teacher. The branding iron teaches that a true disciple bears his Master's mark. Just as a rancher's cattle carry his brand so that everyone knows whose they are, the disciple of Christ carries the Lord's markings upon him, and people can tell whose he is. The deacon's aim is that every soul in his families should bear that unmistakable mark of belonging to Christ, branded as the Lord's own.

sa.prompt: Explain the first mark of a disciple, commitment, and the lesson of the stagecoach.
sa.model: The first mark of a disciple is commitment. To declare love for God means nothing without commitment behind it, and the great danger is a religion that is wide but shallow, like a river a mile wide and an inch deep. A committed Christian is an active one who serves joyfully, out of love and not duty. The stagecoach illustration makes the point: when the coach reached a steep hill, the first-class kept their seats, the second-class got out and walked, but the third-class got out and pushed. The church needs more third-class passengers who will push, and the deacon calls his families to be that kind, chiefly by his own example.

sa.prompt: Explain the second mark, confession, and the two ways it is made.
sa.model: The second mark of a disciple is confession, the open owning of Christ before others. In Matthew 10:32-33 the Lord said that whoever confesses Him before men, He will also confess before His Father, but whoever denies Him He will deny. Confession is made in two ways. It is made by the life, for a witness cannot be divorced from a lifestyle, and in everything a believer does he is drawing people toward Jesus or driving them away. And it is made by the lips, for we must not be too timid or ashamed to tell others plainly of the Lord. The deacon helps his families become bold and consistent confessors.

sa.prompt: Explain the third mark, the cost of discipleship.
sa.model: The third mark of a disciple is a willingness to bear the cost, for following Jesus has never been without cost. The world that hated the Master hates His disciples too. That cost may touch our families, since Christ came not to bring peace but a sword and can set a believer at odds with his own household. It may touch our worldly interests, for if we love anything more than the Lord, He may ask us to lay it down. And it may touch even life itself, as the Salvation Army officers showed when they gave their life belts to others, saying they could die better. The deacon strengthens his families to count this cost honestly.

sa.prompt: Why is honest teaching about the cost an act of love?
sa.model: Honest teaching about the cost is an act of love because it gives a disciple roots that will hold. A deacon who promises his families an easy, comfortable Christianity sets them up to stumble at the very first hardship, when reality does not match the promise. But one who tells them the truth, that the path is glorious yet not always easy, prepares them to endure. He does not frighten them away from Christ; rather he readies them to follow Him all the way home. A disciple who has counted the cost beforehand will not fall away when the trouble finally comes.

sa.prompt: Why is the deacon, as a layman, so well placed to evangelize his families?
sa.model: The deacon, as a layman, is well placed to evangelize his families for two reasons. First, most people come to Christ not through a stranger but through a friend; of the many healed by Jesus in the Gospels, the great majority were brought to Him by others, and the deacon, who knows his families and has their trust, is exactly such a friend. Second, a layman often has an access no preacher enjoys. The witnessing plumber won hundreds to Christ, and a minister said that many will listen to a workingman who will not listen to a preacher. The deacon is a workingman among workingmen.

sa.prompt: How does Luke 19:10 shape the deacon's burden for the lost?
sa.model: Luke 19:10 says that the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost, and this shapes the deacon's whole burden for the lost. He shares his Master's heart, which is set on seeking the perishing. So he never assumes that everyone in his families already knows Christ, for most people do not. He remembers that the unsaved loved ones among his families will one day face eternity, and that Jesus is not merely an answer but the only answer. Because his Lord came to seek and to save, the deacon also goes seeking the lost entrusted to his care.

sa.prompt: Describe how the deacon goes about seeking the lost among his families.
sa.model: The deacon seeks the lost among his families by patient, loving, personal work. He watches for open doors and builds the relationship warmly, knowing that he may sow for years before he reaps. He prays for the lost by name. He speaks of Christ personally and plainly as the Spirit gives opportunity, never pushy yet never silent, and like Andrew bringing his brother Simon, he brings them to the Savior. He keeps the door open and the relationship warm, remembering that in the end it is God who saves, but that God is pleased to use a faithful friend to bring the lost within reach of His grace.

sa.prompt: Summarize the deacon's ministry of discipleship and evangelism.
sa.model: The deacon's ministry of discipleship and evangelism is the highest reach of his care, going all the way to the soul. By discipleship he labors to form true disciples among his believing families, marked by commitment, by confession, and by a willingness to bear the cost. By evangelism he seeks the lost among his families, sharing the gospel as a trusted friend so they may come to Christ. He longs to see every soul bear the Lord's mark, the saved growing strong and the lost brought home. In this he obeys the Great Commission, making disciples not among far nations but among the families given to his care.
